This is assuming you verified the iso you downloaded, everything installed without problems, and you're now having problems booting after you've removed the installation media.

Boot up the computer completely, go into a terminal with Ctrl+Alt+F2, login, check for errors in dmesg, do a sudo apt-get update and sudo apt-get dist-upgrade (this will upgrade your programs and kernel,) reboot. If you're still getting a black screen after updating, check for errors in dmesg in the terminal.

To test if it's a video driver problem, enable nomodeset in grub (If you couldn't log in with ctrl+alt+F2, remove quiet and splash to see what errors come up during boot) If nomodeset gets you to the desktop, install the binary drivers for your card.

Other stuff to check in the terminal:

  • df -h - make sure the device "/" under "Mounted on" isn't 100% in use
  • systemctl- page down/up through it and see if there's any errors. If there are, you can get more info with systemctl status name_of_thing_with_errors
  • cat /var/log/Xorg.0.log - check for any errors
  • lspci | grep VGA - the video card model number, if you have an intel and nvidia card: there's special optimus stuff you may have to look into (disabling one video card in the bios)
  • lspci -v - search through the output for the VGA line in the previous command to see the kernel driver in use
